FOREWORD This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Nuclear Materials Sectional Committee had been approved by the Chemical Division Council. Boron compounds are used for controlling the rate of nuclear reactions in the nuclear reactors and thus playa very crucial role in reactor control. The material must therefore meet criteria like isotopic composition. impurity content. There is no ISO Standard on the subject. The standard is formulated based on the indigenous manufacturers' datal practices prevalent in the field in India, The composition of the Committee responsible for the formulation of this standard is given in Annex F. For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with. the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 'Rules for rounding off numerical values (revisedv. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

5 PACKING AND MARKING 5.1 Marking - The containers shall besecurely closed and bear legibly and inde libly the follow ing particulars: a) Name of the material; b) Min imum assay and maximum impurit y concentration; c) Gross and net mass; d) Date of manufacture and batch number; and e) Name of the manufacturer and his recognized trade-mark, if any.

13320 : 1992

3 TERMINOLOGY For the purpose of this standard. the following definitions shall apply. 3.1 Nuclear Reactor - A de vice in which a selfsustaining nuclear fission reaction can be maintained and controlled. 3.2 Reactor Control - The intentional variations of the rea ct ion rate in a nuclear rea ctor obtained by adju stment of reactivity to achieve or mainta in a des ired state of operation . 4 REQUIREMENTS 4.1 General- The material shall be in the form of white crystalline powder. free from odour. dirt. foreign matter and visible impurities.

5.1.1 BIS Cenification Marking - The product may also be marked with the Standard Mark .
5.1.1.1 The use of the Standard Mark is gov erned by the provi sions of the Bureau of Indian Standards A cr. 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The deta ils of conditions under which the licence for the use of Standard Mark ma y be gr an te d to manu facturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards ,

IS 15810 : 2008 5.2 Packing - Unless otherwise agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier, the powder shall be packed in suitable containers such as HDPE bottles and sealed under IT:.... isture-proof conditions. 6 SAMPLING AND CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY 6.1 The samples shall be collected according to the method in IS 8883 (Part 1) and with the help of the equipment prescribed in IS 8883 (Part 2). 6.2 Criteria for Conformity 6.2.1 Sampling plans to meet acceptance criteria and inspection and measurement procedures that describe the method of compl iance with this specification shall be established by the seller and submitted to the buyer for approval. 6.2.2 Each sample taken shall be sufficient to perform the following in the event they are necessary or desired by the buyer : a) Quality verification tests by the seller, b) Acceptance tests by the buyer, c) Referee tests in the event these become necessary. and d) Retention of archive samples by the seller. 6.3 Archive samples shall be retained by the seller for a period of time specified by the buyer and delivered to the buyer upon request.

ANNEXA
(Clause 4.2.1)
THERMAL IONIZATION MASS SPECTROMETRIC METHOD FOR THE DETERMINATION OF THE ISOTOPIC CONTENT OF BORON A-I APPARATUS A-I.I Thermal Ionization Mass Spectrometer A-2 REAGENTS A-2.1 Demineralized Water A-2.2 Sodium Carbonate A-3 PROCEDURE Dissolve 5 .58 mg of lithium pentaborate in demineralized water. Warm, if necessary. Dilute to get a concentration of 1 ppm of boron. 2 ml of this solution (containing 21lg of B) is treated with a known amount of sodium carbonate to maintain atom ratio of B : Na equal to 1:1. The treated sample is evaporated under infrared lamp to get sodium tetraborate. The residue is redissolved in demineralized water and concentrated into a tiny drop. Using a capillary this drop is carefully loaded on a degassed rhenium/tantalum filament. Pass about 0.8 A current through the filament to dry the sample on the filament. Then momentarily increase the filament current to about 1.6 A to dull red heat. The loaded fi lament is taken into the ion source of the thermal ionization mass spectrometer. After the pressure in the mass spectrometer becomes less than 10-6 mb, the filament is electrically heated slowly to about 0.8 to 1.2 A (700-900'C) . Thermal ionization of the sample results in the formation of NazBOz+ions and after optimising the focusing and other analysis parameters, the NazBO/ molecular ions at mlz 88 and 89 corresponding to 10B+ and IIB+ are mass analysed by the magnetic analyser of the mass spectrometer. The ion intensities are measured by a suitable detector (Faraday cup or electron multiplier or Daly scintillation detector). The ratio of the ion intensities gives the atom ratio of lOS/liB. From this isotopic composition can be calculated. A-4 CALCULATION

ANNEXC
[Table 1,51 No. (ii)]
SPECTROPHOTOMETRIC DETERMINATION OF CHLORIDE IN LITHIUM PENTABORATE C-1 PRINCIPLE A known weight of the sample is heated to I lOO"C in a current to steam. The hydrogen chloride formed is collected in the condensate, and the chloride is determined by spectrophotometry after the addition of mercuric thiocyanate and ferric alum. C-2 REAGENTS C-2 .1 Double Distilled Water - Freshl y distilled water is used throughout the experiment. C-2.2 Ferric Alum Solution (12 Percent) - Dissolve 120 g of ferric alum salt in 430 ml of boiling water. Add with stirring 500 ml of hot nitric acid. Gently heat the solution until complete dis solution. Make the solution to I 000 ml. C-2.3 Mercuric Thiocyanate Solution (4 Percent) Dissolve 4 g of recrystallized mercuric thiocyanate in I 000 ml of ethyl alcohol. C-3 PROCEDURE A known weight of the sample in powder form is taken in a silica reaction tube and is heated to I lOO"C. A constant current of steam is passed over the sample. On pyrohydrolysis, hydrogen chloride is formed which is then collected along with the condensed stearn in a collection tube. About 80-90 ml of the condensate is collected. This is then concentrated to about 20 ml. About 2 ml each offerric alum and mercuric thiocyanate are added and the total volume is made up to 25 ml. The solution is allowed to stand for 20 min and then absorbance is measured at 480 nm against a reagent blank. Construct a calibration plot between the known amount of chloride and the absorbance by talcing a series of standard samples containing known concentration of chloride in the range I to lOOppmw.The concentration of chloride can then be read from the calibration plot .
